transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We're here to review the redaction gateway rollout scheduled to begin tomorrow morning. As a reminder, the gateway removes payment-card and government-ID fields from request logs before they reach the customer-support observability system, and it passed its functional and synthetic traffic tests in staging. Before I can sign off, I need all four review entries — backend engineering, reliability, customer support, and security. Let's start with any blocking findings. If you have a blocking finding, please record it as a formal checklist finding now, before we move into general discussion.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for the backend engineering review. While helping migrate an unrelated client SDK this afternoon, I confirmed that exactly eight legacy clients — Lark, Meridian, Osprey, Quill, Radian, Solace, Timber, and Vale — still require the unredacted field format. The gateway must initially exclude exactly those clients, or we risk breaking their integrations. I have not yet updated the rollout ticket with this information.

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for the reliability review. My traffic replay this morning showed that the currently provisioned redaction workers can safely process exactly 25% of expected peak traffic, or about 450 requests per second, while preserving the team's 500-requests-per-second headroom target. I have not posted the result because the capacity dashboard is being rebuilt. At current provisioning, we are far short of the capacity we need for a production rollout.

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for the customer support review. While checking an account escalation, I confirmed that Acme's contract requires 72 hours of notice before any production change that alters the format of data available to its support team. The redaction gateway will alter the format of data available to support, Acme has not been notified, and I have not added this clause to the launch checklist. Since the rollout is scheduled for tomorrow morning, we cannot meet the 72-hour notice requirement in time.

During a compliance review today, I confirmed that redaction decisions for payment-related requests must be recorded in immutable storage for exactly 400 days, and the gateway must fail closed on payment endpoints if redaction is unavailable. This finding is still in my review notes rather than a filed ticket, so it has not yet been captured in the launch checklist.

commitments.detail: Update the rollout ticket with the eight legacy clients requiring exclusion: Lark, Meridian, Osprey, Quill, Radian, Solace, Timber, and Vale.
Post the capacity finding to the launch checklist once the dashboard is available, and provision additional redaction workers to meet the 500-requests-per-second headroom target before any rollout.
Add Acme's 72-hour notice clause to the launch checklist and initiate notification to Acme so the clock starts; Acme traffic must remain excluded until the 72-hour notice period is satisfied.

File a formal ticket capturing the immutable storage retention requirement of 400 days for payment-related redaction decisions and the fail-closed requirement for payment endpoints, and add both to the launch checklist.
Rollout is blocked until all four blocking findings are resolved, recorded in the checklist, and a re-review is completed. Tomorrow morning's rollout will not proceed.
